mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lifts the no-duplicate-per-(application,eventType) constraint; injecting two indistinguishable audit entries for the same application+event forces a counterexample within the Alloy scope, which both append-only assertions must detect.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: AuditEntry | e1.application = e2.application and e1.eventType = e2.eventType }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets Alloy invent an Operation whose (role, kind) is not in the permission matrix; the injection forces a customer-issued PostDecision, which is a denied cell, so both the catalogue LeastPrivilege check and the staff-only-decision FR must fail.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = Customer and op.kind = PostDecision }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets an application exist without a Submitted audit entry; injection forces such an application into existence within scope, so both the per-application Submitted-event check and the audit-completeness pattern must fail.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some a: LoanApplication | (no e: AuditEntry | e.application = a and e.eventType = Submitted) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lifts the customer/own-resource gate on GetApplicationById; the injection constructs an Operation where a customer successfully sees another customer's application, which is exactly the leak FR-013 and the two patterns must catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = Customer and op.kind = GetApplicationById and some op.target and op.target.customer != op.caller and op.visibleResult = True }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets an unauthenticated Operation reach a handler; the injection forces existence of an op with authenticated=False, which both auth-required assertions must reject.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthViolation { some op: Operation | op.authenticated = False }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets one customer hold two simultaneous Pending Review applications; the injection makes two such applications co-exist for the same customer, which violates the partial unique index and so the FR-005 assertion.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OnePendingViolation { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.customer = a2.customer and a1.status = PendingReview and a2.status = PendingReview }
